Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Fluency, part of Garden Suggested vocabulary fruits, vegetables, grow, energy, healthy, soil, cro in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we improve our reading speed? 2. How do we show feelings and emotions when reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. pick out words with target letter-sound combinations /tw/ , /wh/, /ɪə/, /θ/, /ð/ from a chart/braille chart.

2. read words containing the target letter- sound combinations correctly.

3. read a text displaying the right facial expressions and tonal variations for learners with low vision. Learners with blindness to be given a 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. pick out words with target letter-sound combinations /tw/ , /wh/, /ɪə/, /θ/, /ð/ from a chart/braille chart.
2. read words containing the target letter- sound combinations correctly.
3. read a text displaying the right facial expressions and tonal variations for learners with low vision. Learners with blindness to be given a 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn; the learner’s independent reading skills are enhanced as they practice reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable

words.

Values:
Unity is developed as the learner works collaboratively with peers during group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem); the learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they acquire reading fluency skills.

Link to other learning areas

Reading fluency is also emphasized in Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages Activities.

lines or stanzas of a poem.
